chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani and Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim al-Hamadani, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and asked him about a woman who rented out her property for ten years, on the condition that she would be given the rent at the end of each year, and nothing of the rent would be advanced to her unless the time had passed. She died three years before or after that time. Is it obligatory upon her heirs to enforce the lease until the time, or does the lease become terminated by the death of the woman?

So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'If there was a specified time for her which had not yet reached and she died, then that lease is for her heirs. If that time had not yet reached, and a third of it had, or half of it, or something from it, then her heirs would be given in accordance with whatever had reached from that time, God willing.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a land lease if the owner dies before the agreed term ends?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the lease contract (ijarah) is a property right that survives the lessor's death, ensuring continuity for the lessee. The ruling distinguishes between the right to the remaining term and the proportional compensation for the elapsed period, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that death does not automatically void ongoing contractual obligations. This hadith serves as a foundational text for inheritance law regarding unexpired leases in Shia fiqh.
